source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And he spoke to them a teaching [or: matter]: a person is obligated always to pray and not to sin [or: miss the mark]. And Yeshua was walking through Jericho.

translation_notes: ואומר (consonants אמר): The only Strong's candidate given is H201 (Omar, a proper name), but the consonants אמר universally function as the verb 'to say' (H559). The participle form אומר means 'saying/said.' Chose H559 because the context demands a speech verb introducing a teaching.

להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they/them'. The prepositional ל + הם naturally reads 'to them.' Chose H1992 because this is a standard indirect object construction following a speech verb.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a noun following the verb of speech, 'a word/matter' fits naturally. Chose H1697.

אדם: Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. In a general moral statement about obligation, 'a person/human being' is the natural reading. Chose H120.
textual_notes: The word חייב is not in the provided Strong's candidates; it appears to be a later Hebrew/Aramaic legal term meaning 'obligated/liable.' This is characteristic of Mishnaic Hebrew rather than Biblical Hebrew.
להתפלל is a hitpael infinitive of פלל (to pray) — no Strong's candidates were provided, but the form is standard.
לחתטוא appears to be an unusual spelling of לחטוא (to sin), with an extra ת. This may reflect a dialectal or scribal variant.
הולך — no Strong's candidates provided; standard qal participle of הלך (to walk/go).

verses.literal: And [he] said to them [a] word: obligated [is] a man always to pray and not to sin. And Yeshua [was] walking in Jericho.

verses.translation: He says: There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear [or: revere] God, and he had no fear or shame before people. And behold, a certain man came — his name [was] Zakkai — who was chief of the tax-collectors [or: customs officials], and he was exceedingly [or: greatly] wealthy.

translation_notes: בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'a watcher/angel', H5895 'a young ass'. The preposition ב + עיר in context of a judge sitting in a locale clearly points to 'city.' Chose H5892.
היה (first): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. A copular verb introducing a character ('there was a judge') requires 'to be.' Chose H1961.

ירא: Candidates: H3372 'to fear/revere', H3373 'fearing/reverent'. After שאינו (who does not), a verb infinitive/participle is expected. Both work; chose H3372 as the verbal form fits after the negation construction.
והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. The narrative shift introducing a new character is classic use of הנה as 'behold.' Chose H2009.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act manly'. As a noun subject, 'a man' is the natural reading. Chose H376.
אחד (both instances): Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Used as an adjective modifying nouns (judge, city, man), 'one/a certain' is standard. Chose H259.
שהיה: ש (relative particle 'who') + היה. Candidates for היה: H1961 'to be', H1962 'ruin'. A relative clause describing Zakkai's role requires 'who was.' Chose H1961.
שר: Candidates: H8269 'a head person/chief', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. Describing someone's role/rank, 'chief' is coherent. Chose H8269.

מן: Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from/out of', H4482 'musical chord'. After 'shame' the preposition 'from' (indicating source/cause of shame) fits naturally. Chose H4480.
textual_notes: דיין is not in the provided Strong's; it is a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'judge' (related to דין, H1777).
אחת — feminine form of אחד, no separate Strong's provided; it modifies עיר (feminine noun).
שאינו — compound: ש (relative) + אינו (he is not), a characteristic Mishnaic Hebrew construction. No Strong's provided.
א0להים — the 0 appears to be a scribal peculiarity or manuscript damage in place of the expected ל, reading אלהים (God/H430).
ובושת — ו + בושת, 'and shame.' Related to בוש (H954, to be ashamed). The noun form בשת/בושת is attested but no Strong's candidate was provided.
האתנשים — appears anomalous. Likely a corruption or variant spelling of האנשים ('the men/people,' from איש H376/אנוש). The extra ת may be a scribal error.
ש״מו — the ״ mark appears to be a scribal abbreviation indicator; reading שמו 'his name' (from שם H8034 + possessive suffix).

העולמיים — This is puzzling. The root עולם (H5769) means 'eternity/world.' However, in context of a tax-chief, this likely reflects a Hebrew rendering of a term for 'tax-collectors' or 'publicans' — possibly a creative coinage meaning 'worldly ones' or 'those dealing with worldly/civic affairs.' This is not a standard Biblical Hebrew term.

verses.literal: [He] says: A judge one was in a city one who did not fear God and not was to him fear and shame from the people. And behold came a man one, his name Zakkai, who was chief of the tax-collectors, and he was rich great.

verses.translation: And a certain widow was in that city, and she came to him saying: Judge [or: look into] the matter that is between me and my adversary. And he was greatly desiring to see Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] — what sort of man he was — and he was not able to see him because of the great crowd of people, for that Zakkai was small in stature [or: form].

translation_notes: בעיר: Same as section 2 — 'in the city.' Chose H5892.
שהוא: Candidates for הוא: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. As a pronoun in a relative clause 'that he [is],' chose H1931.
והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. Narrative past 'and he was' introducing his desire. Chose H1961.

חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/be pleased with/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire/matter'. As a verb after היה describing an ongoing state of desire, the verbal form fits. Chose H2654.
מאד: Candidates: H3966 'vehemently/greatly', H108 'a fog'. Modifying desire, 'greatly' is the obvious fit. Chose H3966.

משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'shrubbery'. Following the proper name Yeshua as a title, 'Messiah/Anointed' is the natural reading. Chose H4899.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Combined with זה, the phrase אי זה forms 'which/what sort of' — an interrogative. Chose H335.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. As part of the interrogative phrase אי זה ('which this'), chose H2088.
איש: H376 'a man.' Standard use. Chose H376.
הוא: H1931 'he.' Completing the question 'which man he [is].' Chose H1931.
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5972 same, H5973 'with', H5974 'with'. After רוב ('multitude of'), 'the people' is coherent. Chose H5971.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because/for/that'. Introducing a causal clause explaining why he couldn't see. Chose H3588.
היה: H1961 'was.' Describing Zakkai's physical state. Chose H1961.
textual_notes: This section appears to interleave TWO narratives: the parable of the unjust judge and the widow (verses about the widow coming to the judge) and the story of Zakkai in Jericho (his desire to see Yeshua). The manuscript seems to weave them together or transition mid-section.
ובאה — the candidate H872 'an entrance to a building' doesn't fit; this is clearly the qal perfect feminine of בוא (to come, H935) with vav conjunction. The form is standard.

נראה — could be niphal imperative of ראה ('let it be seen/judge my case') or niphal perfect ('it was seen'). In context of a legal plea, the imperative reading ('look into/judge') fits the widow's petition.
מעניין — not in Strong's candidates. This appears to be מ + עניין (matter/affair), a post-biblical Hebrew word related to ענה. It reads 'regarding the matter.'

ביני ושכנגדי — 'between me and the one who is against me.' These are Mishnaic Hebrew legal terms. בין + suffix 'between me,' and ש + כ + נגד + suffix 'the one who is opposite/against me' (i.e., my legal adversary).
ק טן appears to be קטן (small) split across a line break or damaged in the manuscript. Reading as one word קטן (H6996, small).
The transition from the widow's story to Zakkai's story is abrupt; this may reflect the manuscript combining Luke 18:1-8 material with Luke 19:1-10 material.

verses.literal: And a widow one was in the city that and she came to him saying: be seen regarding [the] matter that [is] between me and [the one] against me. And he was desiring greatly to see Yeshua Messiah — which this man he [is] — and not [he] was able to see him on account of [the] multitude of the people for that Zakkai was small [of] form.

verses.translation: And he was not willing to act [or: to do justice]. And much time passed. And afterward he said in his heart: Even though I do not fear God or people — And he ran and climbed up into a certain tree, its name [was] sycamore, so that he could see Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah], for there he was [about] to pass by.

translation_notes: ועבר: Candidates: H5674 'to cross over/pass', H5675 'a region across', H5676 'opposite side', H5677 'Eber (name)'. As a verb describing time passing, 'passed' is the natural reading. Chose H5674.
זמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2164 'to agree on a time', H2165 'an appointed occasion', H2166 same. As a noun ('time passed'), the nominal form fits. Chose H2165.
רב: Candidates: H7227 'abundant/much', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant', H7230 'abundance'. Modifying זמן (time), 'much' is the obvious reading. Chose H7227.

ואחר: Candidates: H309 'to loiter/delay', H310 'after/afterward', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher (name)'. Following 'much time passed,' 'and afterward' is the logical continuation. Chose H310.
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same, H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. As the main verb introducing speech, chose H559.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'a mother', H518 'if/although/even if'. Introducing a concessive clause ('even if I don't fear...'), chose H518.
ירא: H3372 'to fear' or H3373 'fearing.' After שאיני ('that I do not'), the verbal form works. Chose H3372.
ועלה: Candidates: H5927 'to ascend/go up', H5928 'holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'a step/holocaust', H5931 'a pretext'. After running, climbing a tree is the coherent physical action. Chose H5927.
שקמה: Candidates: H8256 'sycamore tree', H7054 'a stalk of grain'. Identifying a tree one climbs, 'sycamore' is the only sensible reading. Chose H8256.
בעבור (first): H5668 'on account of/in order that' or H5669 'stored grain'. Purpose clause ('so that he could see') requires the adverbial use. Chose H5668.
יוכל: The only candidate H3116 is 'Jukal (a name),' but the consonants יכל clearly represent the verb 'to be able' (H3201). In context 'so that he could see,' this is the imperfect of יכל.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'a name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. In the clause 'for there he was to pass,' the adverb 'there' fits. Chose H8033.
כי: H3587 'brand/scar' or H3588 'because/for'. Introducing reason clause. Chose H3588.
היה: H1961 'to be' — 'it was for him to pass.' Chose H1961.

לעבור: H5668 'on account of' or H5669 'stored grain'. But this is actually the infinitive of עבר (H5674, to pass/cross over) with ל prefix — 'to pass by.' Chose the verbal root H5674 for the infinitive.
textual_notes: This section again interleaves two narratives: the judge's internal monologue (from the parable of the unjust judge) and Zakkai climbing the sycamore tree (from the Zakkai story). The judge's speech appears to break off mid-sentence (the sentence beginning 'even if I do not fear God and people' lacks a conclusion in this section).
לעתשות — unusual spelling, likely לעשות (to do/make), infinitive of עשה (H6213). The extra ת may be a scribal peculiarity of this manuscript.

ורץ — The candidate H7518 'a fragment' doesn't fit; the consonants רץ also represent the qal participle/perfect of רוץ (H7323, to run). In context of rushing to climb a tree, 'ran' is the clear reading.
בלבו — ב + לב (heart, H3820) + suffix ו — 'in his heart.' Standard Hebrew idiom for internal thought.
שאיני — ש + אין + suffix, 'that I am not' — Mishnaic Hebrew construction.
ואתנשים — same anomalous form as section 2, likely meaning 'and people/men.'
שמו — could be read as 'its name' (the tree's name) or 'his name.' Context suggests 'its name' referring to the tree species.

verses.literal: And not [he] was willing to do. And passed time much. And after [he] said in his heart: even if I do not fear God and people — and [he] ran and went up in a tree one, its name sycamore, in order that [he] could see Yeshua Messiah, for there it was for him to pass.

verses.translation: Indeed, lest [or: when] this widow keeps coming to me in the end, she will make a mockery [or: laughingstock] of me. And when Yeshua came to the place, Zakkai looked up and Yeshua the Anointed One [Messiah] saw [him] and said to him: Zakkai, come down quickly and hurry, for I am compelled [or: it is necessary] that I come today into your house.

translation_notes: לעג: Candidates: H3932 'to deride/mock', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'a buffoon/foreigner'. After תעשה ('she will make'), a noun object is expected — 'she will make mockery.' Chose H3933.

ממני: The candidates given are H4507 'Fate idol', H4508 'Minni (province)', H5204 'lamentation'. However, ממני is standardly מן (H4480, from) + suffix ני (me) = 'from me/of me.' Chose H4480 as the prepositional base.

וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With כ prefix and ו conjunction, כאשר means 'when/as.' Chose H834.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H409 same, H410 'God/strength', H411 'these/those', H412 same, H413 'to/toward/near'. As a preposition before המקום ('the place'), 'to' is the natural reading. Chose H413.
המקום: Candidates: H4725 'a standing/place/locality', H6965 'to rise', H6966 same. With the article ה, 'the place' is the straightforward nominal reading. Chose H4725.
וראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'a seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh (name)'. As a narrative verb 'and [he] saw,' chose H7200.
משיח: H4899 'anointed/Messiah' vs. H7878-7880 (ponder/shrubbery). Title following Yeshua — chose H4899.

מהר: Candidates: H4116 'to hurry', H4117 'to bargain for a wife', H4118 'hurrying/in a hurry', H4119 'a price for a wife', H2022 'mountain', H2023 'Hor'. As an adverb modifying descent ('come down quickly'), chose H4118.
כי: H3587 'brand/scar' or H3588 'because/for.' Introducing the reason for the command. Chose H3588.
אני: H589 'I' or H590 'a ship/fleet.' First person pronoun in 'I am compelled.' Chose H589.
היום: H3117 'a day' or H3118 'a day.' With article ה, 'the day/today.' Chose H3117.
textual_notes: This section continues the interleaving: the first part completes the judge's internal monologue from the unjust judge parable, then transitions to the Zakkai narrative.
כאתשר — unusual spelling of כאשר (when/as), with an extra ת. Same scribal tendency as לעתשות and תעתשה.
תמצאני — ת (3fs prefix) + מצא (to find, H4672) + ני (me suffix) = 'she will find me.' Standard verbal form.
הבא — could be the participle of בוא 'the coming/next' or simply 'who comes.' In context 'to the end, the coming [one]' it means 'in the end coming [to me]' — i.e., her persistent coming.
תעתשה — unusual spelling of תעשה (she will make), 3fs imperfect of עשה (H6213).
הביט — hiphil perfect of נבט (H5027, to look/behold). 'He looked up.' No candidates were provided.
וחושה — The candidate H2364 'Chushah (name)' doesn't fit. This is likely the imperative of חוש (H2363, to hurry) with ה suffix — 'hurry!' or 'make haste!'
מוכרח — not in Strong's; a post-biblical Hebrew form (hophal participle of כרח) meaning 'compelled/forced/necessary.'
שאבוא — ש (that) + אבוא (1cs imperfect of בוא, H935) = 'that I will come.'
בביתך — ב + בית (H1004) + ך (your suffix) = 'in your house.'

The subject of וראה is ambiguous: it could be 'Zakkai looked up and saw Yeshua' or 'Yeshua saw [Zakkai].' The flow of the narrative (Yeshua then speaks to Zakkai) suggests Yeshua is the one who saw and spoke.

verses.literal: Indeed when the widow this will find me to the end coming she will make mockery of me. And when Yeshua came to the place, Zakkai looked up and saw Yeshua Messiah and said to him: Zakkai, descend quickly and hurry, for compelled [am] I that I will come today in your house.

verses.translation: And our lord said: See what the judge said out of [the] wickedness [or: brokenness] of [his] heart

translation_notes: אמר (both instances): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context requires a verb of speech — 'our lord said' and 'what the judge said'.
מרוע: Root רוע H7321 means 'to mar, to break, to shatter'. With prefix מ this reads 'from the breaking/evil of' — describing the moral corruption motivating the judge's words.
לב: Candidates: H3820/H3821 both mean 'heart'. Chose H3820. 'Evil of heart' describes the judge's corrupt character.
textual_notes: מרוע could be parsed as מ + רוע (from the evil/breaking), functioning as 'out of the wickedness of'. The root רוע H7321 carries both the sense of shattering/marring and, by extension, moral evil. Both senses may be operative here.

verses.literal: And our lord said see what said the judge from evil of heart

verses.translation: And will YHWH not avenge them — they who [are his] chosen ones crying out to him day and night — and will he not have compassion on them?

translation_notes: שהם: Candidates: H7718 'beryl', H7719 'Shoham', or ש + הם H1992 'who/that they'. Chose ש (relative particle) + הם H1992 'they' because the context requires a relative clause: 'they who are chosen ones crying out'.
מהם: מ + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 'them' with preposition מ meaning 'from/for them', referring to the chosen ones.
textual_notes: The clause structure is ambiguous as to whether this is a rhetorical question ('Will YHWH not avenge them?') or a statement ('YHWH will not avenge them'). The parable context of an unjust judge contrasted with God suggests a rhetorical question expecting a positive answer — i.e., God WILL avenge them. The final phrase מהם could mean 'from them' (compassion originating from them) or 'for them' (compassion directed toward them). The latter fits better contextually.

verses.literal: And YHWH not will-avenge them who-they [are] chosen-ones crying-out to-him day and-night and-not will-be to-him compassion from-them

verses.translation: Surely [when] the son of the human being [or: mankind] comes, do you believe he will find faithfulness [or: steadfastness] in the earth?

translation_notes: בן: Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son'. Chose H1121 as 'son of' — part of the construct 'son of the human being'.

האדם: Candidates: H119 'to flush', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 'human being' because בן האדם is a well-attested construct meaning 'son of mankind/the human being'.
א״מונה: The abbreviation mark (״) indicates a scribal contraction. The consonants point to אמונה, from root אמן — 'faithfulness, steadfastness, trustworthiness'.
textual_notes: The relationship between בא (comes) and תאמינו (will you believe) is syntactically ambiguous — it could read 'when the son of man comes, will you believe that he will find...' or 'the son of man comes; will you believe that he will find...' The א״מונה contains a scribal abbreviation mark, reconstructed as אמונה (faithfulness).

verses.literal: Surely son-of the-human-being comes will-you-believe that-he-will-find faithfulness in-the-earth

verses.translation: [And he said] to some [or: a portion] who trust in themselves as [though they were] righteous and despise the others, this [is] the matter [or: word, parable]:

translation_notes: זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative pronoun 'this' fits naturally: 'this is the matter'.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'this is the word/matter' introduces a teaching or parable.
textual_notes: The word ]ואומר[ is bracketed in the source, indicating it was likely a scribal addition or restoration. The phrase זה הדבר could mean 'this is the word/saying' (introducing what follows) or 'this is the matter' (summarizing what precedes). Given that it precedes the parable of two men, it likely introduces the teaching.

verses.literal: [And-he-said] to-some who-trust in-themselves as righteous-ones and-despise the-others this the-word

verses.translation: Two men went up to the sanctuary [or: holy place, temple] to pray — the one [was] a Pharisee [lit: separatist] and the other [was] a worldly man [or: commoner, man of the world]

translation_notes: שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second/double/two'. Chose H8145 because 'two men' is the natural reading before אנשים.

במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', H6942 'to be clean', H6944 'sacred place'. Chose H4720 as the noun with prefix ב: 'in the sanctuary/temple'. The context of going up to pray fits a temple.
האחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 — 'the one' as a distributive pronoun distinguishing the two men.
textual_notes: פרוש — this word means 'separated one / separatist' from the root פרש (to separate). This is the Hebrew term underlying 'Pharisee'. עולמיי — derived from עולם (world/age) with adjectival ending, meaning 'worldly one' or 'man of the world'. This likely renders a concept like 'publican/tax-collector' — someone immersed in worldly affairs — but the Hebrew specifically says 'worldly man'.

verses.literal: Two men went-up in-the-sanctuary to-pray the-one [a] separatist and-the-one [a] worldly-man

verses.translation: And the Pharisee [lit: separatist], standing on his feet, said these words: Lord God, I give thanks [or: grace] to you, for I am not like the other men — robbers, evildoers, and adulterers — and moreover I am not like this worldly man.

translation_notes: על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 'upon' — 'standing upon his feet' is a natural physical description.

אומר: The only Strong's candidate listed is H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants אומר are clearly the qal participle of אמר H559 'to say'. The participle form 'saying' fits the narrative context. Assigning H559.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, אלה also matches the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (typically listed as H428). In context, 'these words' is the natural reading. Using H428 equivalent.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 — addressing God as 'Lord'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Chose H3588 — conjunction 'for/because' introducing the reason for gratitude.
אני (both): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun in a prayer.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative pointing to the worldly man present in the temple.
ועוד: Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'still/moreover', H5751 'still'. Chose H5750 — 'moreover/and still' adds another comparison.
textual_notes: חינות — This appears to be a noun form related to חן (grace/favor). The phrase חינות אני עושה לך could mean 'grace/thanks I give to you' or 'I show grace/favor to you.' In context of a prayer of self-congratulation, 'I give thanks to you' is most natural.
איניני — This is an emphatic negation: אין + אני ('I am not'). The double first-person marking is emphatic.
א״להים contains the abbreviation mark (״), reconstructed as אלהים (God).

אלה: H428 (the demonstrative 'these') is the standard identification but was not listed among the candidates provided. The consonants match. I assign it contextually as 'these' rather than any of the listed candidates which do not fit.

verses.translation: I fast two times in the week; I give a tithe [or: tenth] of all the things that [are] in my possession.

verses.translation: And the worldly man stood at a distance and was not willing to lift his eyes to the heavens, but [was] striking his chest, saying: Lord God, have compassion on me, for I [am] a sinner. And his lord said: See — from [the] evil of heart, from the one who was wronged [or: humbled].

translation_notes: רצה: H7521 'to be pleased with, to be willing'. Fits context — he was not willing to lift his eyes.

לשאת: The candidates listed are H7612 'devastation' and H7613 'elevation/exaltation' for שאת, but this is clearly the infinitive construct of נשא (H5375) 'to lift/carry' with prefix ל. 'To lift his eyes' is the coherent image.

אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (name)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 — adversative particle 'but/however', contrasting his refusal to look up with his chest-beating.
מכה: Candidates: H4347 'wound/blow', or מ + כה H3541 'thus/here'. However, מכה as a participle of נכה (H5221 'to strike') fits perfectly: 'striking his chest'. This is the hiphil participle.
את: Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Chose H853 — direct object marker before חזהו 'his chest'.
אדון: H113 'sovereign/lord' vs H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 — addressing God.
כי: H3587 'scar' vs H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 — 'for I am a sinner'.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'ship'. Chose H589.
ראי: Candidates: H7209 'mirror', H7210 'sight/vision'. Chose H7210 in imperative sense 'see/behold'.
textual_notes: ל6מים contains the same encoding artifact; likely לשמים ('to the heavens').

The final phrases ואדניו ראי מרעלב מהעלב are difficult. ואדניו could be 'and his lord' (i.e., Jesus commenting). מרעלב appears to be מרע + לב ('from evil of heart') echoing section 1. מהעלב could be מ + העלב ('from the offended/humbled one'), from the root עלב meaning 'to wrong/insult'. This may be a scribal note or editorial gloss connecting back to the parable's beginning. The passage is textually uncertain here.
The transition from the worldly man's prayer to ואדניו ראי is abrupt and may indicate a damaged or composite text.

translation_notes: בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'in order that he would touch them'.

שיגע: The candidates listed are from יגע H3021 'to be exhausted/toil'. However, the consonants שיגע also parse as ש + יגע from נגע (H5060) 'to touch/reach'. In context of bringing children so that someone would touch them (lay hands on), H5060 is far more coherent than 'be exhausted in them'.
בהם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 with prefix ב — 'in/on them', referring to the children.
וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 — וכאשר = 'and when'.
זה (first): H2088 'this' vs H2089 'sheep'. Chose H2088 — 'seeing this'.
זה (second): H2088 'this'. Same reasoning — 'prevented this'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', or ל + הם H1992 'to them'. Chose ל + H1992 — 'to them / from them', the disciples forbade the people bringing children.
textual_notes: The final phrase מנעו זה להם is ambiguous: it could mean 'they prevented this from them' (stopped people from bringing children) or 'they forbade this to them' (told the people not to do it). Both yield similar meaning.

שיגע: The listed root יגע (H3021 'to toil/exhaust') does not fit contextually. The reading as ש + נגע (H5060 'to touch') is much more coherent — children brought so he would touch/lay hands on them. The ' mark between בהם and וכאשר may be a section break, punctuation mark, or scribal notation.

verses.translation: And he said to them: Let the little children [or: young ones] come to me and do not hold them back [or: hinder them], for from those like these is the kingdom [or: dominion, reign] of the heavens [or: the ultimate heights].

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the waw-prefixed form with conversive indicates a narrative verb 'and he said.'
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because ל + הם = 'to them,' the standard prepositional phrase in narrative speech introduction.
באלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'nay/if'. Here באלו is a demonstrative 'in/among these,' functioning as a post-biblical Hebrew demonstrative pronoun. H431 is closest as a deictic particle.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as a copular pronoun 'it [is]' linking the preceding clause to 'the kingdom of heavens.'

שמים: Candidates: H8064 'sky/heavens', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heavens' is a coherent domain phrase; 'kingdom of water' or 'kingdom of sea' makes no contextual sense.
textual_notes: מכיוצא is a post-biblical Hebrew compound (מ + כ + יוצא) meaning 'from ones going out like / from such as,' not found in the biblical Strong's lexicon. It functions as 'from ones like these.'
הניחו could derive from נוח (H5117, 'to rest/permit') in the hiphil imperative plural, meaning 'allow/permit.' No Strong's candidate was provided but the root is clear from context.

verses.literal: And he said to them permit the young children the small [ones] to come to me and not you shall prevent them for from [ones] like these it [is] the kingdom [of] the heavens

verses.translation: In truth [or: with certainty] I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom [or: dominion] of the heavens as [or: like] young children will not enter into it.

translation_notes: אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I am saying' is coherent; 'a ship saying' is not.

אומר: The only candidate provided is H201 'Omar' (a proper name). However, the consonants אומר are clearly the qal active participle of אמר (H559) meaning 'saying.' The participle form was not separately listed but derives from the same root.
מי ומי: The doubled interrogative 'who and who' is an idiom for 'whoever' — any and every person.
שלא: The ש prefix is a relative particle ('that/who') + לא (H3808 'not'), forming 'who not' = 'who does not.'
textual_notes: יקבלו and יכנסו are post-biblical Hebrew verb forms (from קבל 'to receive' and כנס 'to enter/gather') not in the biblical Strong's lexicon but well attested in Mishnaic Hebrew.
The phrase מי ומי שלא could be parsed as 'whoever does not' (collective) or as two separate questions. Context demands a universal conditional: 'whoever does not.'

verses.translation: And a certain ruler [or: official] from the Pharisees asked him, saying: Good Rabbi [or: Teacher], what shall I do so that I may inherit life [that is] everlasting [or: eternal]?

translation_notes: ושר: Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. Chose H8269 because a ruler asking a question is coherent; 'a string from the Pharisees' is not.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one ruler' = 'a certain ruler' makes narrative sense.
טוב: Candidates: H2895 'to be/make good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun)'. Chose H2896 as an adjective modifying 'Rabbi' — 'Good Rabbi.'
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the context requires a speech verb introducing the quoted words.
textual_notes: שאלו could be parsed as ש + אלו ('that these') using H431/H432, but contextually it is clearly the verb שאל ('to ask') with 3ms suffix — 'asked him.' The candidate listing for אלו is a red herring here.
מהפרושים is a post-biblical compound: מן + ה + פרושים ('from the Pharisees'). פרושים is not in Strong's biblical lexicon.
נצחיים derives from נצח (H5331 'perpetuity/everlasting') with an adjectival ים ending, meaning 'everlasting/eternal.' Not separately listed in Strong's.
חיים could be plural 'lives' or intensive 'fullness of life.' The ים ending here likely conveys the intensive sense of life in its fullness, as is standard biblical usage.

translation_notes: המצות: The candidate H4695 'a quarrel' doesn't fit; the context demands 'commandments.' The word מצוות (from צוה H6680) is the standard plural of מצוה (H4687 'commandment'). H4695 shares consonants but 'you know the quarrels' makes no sense when followed by a list of prohibitions.

שקר: Candidates: H8265 'to ogle/blink', H8266 'to cheat/be untrue', H8267 'an untruth/sham', H7119 'cool', H7120 'cold'. Chose H8267 because 'testimony of falsehood' = 'false testimony' is coherent; 'testimony of cold' or 'testimony of ogling' is not.

textual_notes: המצות: The Strong's candidate provided (H4695 'quarrel') does not match the context. The word is almost certainly the plural of מצוה (H4687 'commandment'), which was not listed among the candidates. I have assigned H4687 based on the consonantal root and context.

The apostrophe/scribal mark following may indicate a textual note or abbreviation (perhaps for 'you shall not murder' — לא תרצח — which appears to be missing from this list of commandments).

The ordering of commandments here (covet, adultery, steal, false testimony, honor parents) differs from the standard Decalogue order, and 'you shall not murder' appears absent — the scribal mark ' may indicate an omission or abbreviation.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua heard that matter [or: word], he said to him: You still lack one thing. Sell what [or: that which] you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens [or: the heights]. Then come and walk [or: go] after me.

translation_notes: והדבר: Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'word/matter/thing'. Chose H1697 because 'and the word/matter that' is a natural narrative construction; 'the vizier that' has no contextual support.
ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1933 'to be'. With the article ה prefixed, this is the demonstrative 'that (one)' — 'the matter, that one' = 'that matter.' Chose H1931.
שמע: Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8087 'Shema (name)', H8088 'something heard'. Chose H8085 because 'Yeshua heard' is the narrative verb needed here.
דבר: Candidates: H1697 'word/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 — 'you lack one thing' is coherent.
אשר: Candidates: H834 'who/which/what', H833 'to be straight', H836 'Asher'. Chose H834 — 'sell what is yours' requires the relative pronoun.

אחרי: The only candidate provided is H317 'other.' However, the consonants אחרי commonly represent H310 (אחרי 'after/behind'). 'Go after me' = 'follow me' is the coherent reading; 'go other me' is not. Assigning H310.
מכור: Candidate H3564 'furnace/pot' for כור. However, מכור here is the infinitive absolute or imperative of מכר (H4376 'to sell'). 'Sell what you have' is coherent; 'furnace what you have' is not.
textual_notes: ב<מים: The < character appears to be a scribal corruption or lacuna. The expected reading is בשמים ('in the heavens,' ב + H8064). The missing consonant(s) before מים likely represent ש, yielding שמים.
אחרי: H317 'other' was the only candidate provided, but the standard reading is H310 'after/behind.' The phrase ולך אחרי = 'and go after me' is a standard call to discipleship.
מכור: The candidate for כור (H3564 'furnace') does not fit. The word is clearly from מכר (H4376 'to sell') — an imperative 'sell!'
עדיין is post-biblical Hebrew for 'still/yet,' not in Strong's biblical lexicon.
חסרת is from חסר (H2637 'to lack/be without'), 2ms perfect — 'you have lacked / you lack.'

אי: Candidates: H335 'where?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'howler', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H336 'not' because אי + איפשר = 'not possible' = 'impossible.' This is a standard post-biblical Hebrew construction.
שיש: Candidates: H7893 'marble/white', H3426 'there is/are'. Chose H3426 because ש + יש = 'that there is' — 'those that have' is coherent; 'those that marble' is not.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them,' completing 'that there is to them' = 'who have.'

הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as copular pronoun 'it [is]' in the predicate 'more easy it is.'
textual_notes: נקל: This appears to be from קלל (H7043 'to be light/easy') in niphal or a related form. 'Easy/light' is the contextual meaning. Not in the provided candidates.
המחט: From מחט (not in Strong's biblical lexicon as a standalone), meaning 'needle' — a well-known post-biblical Hebrew word. The ה is the definite article.
שיעבור: ש + יעבור = 'that will pass through,' from עבר (H5674 'to cross over/pass through').

translation_notes: אלה (consonants א-ל-ה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, in context 'these the-words' demands a demonstrative pronoun; the consonants אלה also correspond to H428 (אֵלֶּה, 'these'), which is the standard demonstrative. None of the listed candidates fit as well as the demonstrative pronoun reading. Chose H428 (unlisted but consonantally identical) because 'these words' is the only coherent reading.

יוכל (consonants י-ו-כ-ל): Candidate: H3116 'Jukal, an Israelite name'. However, in context 'and who Jukal to be saved' is nonsensical. The consonants י-כ-ל correspond to the verb H3201 'to be able, to prevail', with יוכל being a standard imperfect form. Chose H3201 because 'who is able to be saved' is the only coherent reading.
נושע (consonants נ-ו-ש-ע): This is a nifal participle from ישע (H3467, 'to save/deliver'). The passive form means 'saved/delivered'.
textual_notes: אלה: The provided candidates do not include the demonstrative pronoun H428, but the consonants are identical. Context demands the demonstrative reading.
יוכל: The only provided candidate is the proper name Jukal (H3116), but the consonants clearly support the common verb יכל (H3201, 'to be able') in imperfect form.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, "The things [that are] impossible for a human being [are] possible for God. You shall not covet... all that [belongs] to your neighbor, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."

translation_notes: אמר (consonants א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Context demands a speech verb introducing a quote. Chose H559.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', or ל + הם H1992 'they/them'. Context 'said to them' requires the prepositional phrase ל + הם. Chose H1992.

לאדם (consonants א-ד-ם): Candidates: H119 'flush', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. The phrase 'the impossible for a human being' demands the generic noun for humanity. Chose H120.

לאל (consonants א-ל): Candidates: H3815 'Lael', H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Context contrasts what is impossible for humans with what is possible for God. Chose ל + H410 'God'.
אשר (consonants א-ש-ר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Used as relative pronoun 'that/which'. Chose H834.
textual_notes: The text appears to combine two separate teachings: one about impossibility/possibility with God, and commandments about coveting and loving one's neighbor. The ellipsis after תחמד suggests missing text.
ואהבתלרעךכמוך appears to be written as a single string, representing 'and-you-shall-love-your-neighbor-as-yourself' — a well-known compound phrase from Leviticus 19:18.

verses.translation: And Kepha [Peter] said, "Behold, we have left all things and we are going [or: walking] after you."

translation_notes: אמר: Same analysis as before. Speech verb in narrative context. Chose H559.
הנה (consonants ה-נ-ה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. The interjection 'behold' fits a declarative statement opening. Chose H2009.
כל (consonants כ-ל): H3605 'the whole/all' vs H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Hebrew context. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: וכיפא is not in the Strong's dictionary; this is an Aramaic proper name (Kepha/Cephas/Peter), indicating the text uses later Hebrew or is a translation from Aramaic.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to them, "Truly I say to you, no human being will leave his father and his mother, or his brothers, or his wife, or his sons, or the houses of his dwelling, for the sake of the kingdom of YHWH,"

translation_notes: שום (consonants ש-ו-ם): Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7761 (Aramaic), H7762 'garlic'. In later Hebrew שום functions as an indefinite determiner ('any/some'); combined with לא it means 'no' (no human). Chose H7760 as the base form that evolved into this usage.
אדם: Same as section 2. Generic human being. Chose H120.
אני (consonants א-נ-י): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Context 'truth I am saying' requires first person pronoun. Chose H589.
אומר: The listed candidate H201 'Omar' is a proper name. However, consonants א-מ-ר are clearly a participle of H559 'to say'. Chose H559 (participle form).

אחיו: Listed candidate H283 'Achio (proper name)'. However, consonants א-ח-י-ו clearly read as אָחִיו 'his brother(s)' from H251 (אָח, 'brother') with 3ms suffix. Chose H251 because the list of family members demands 'his brothers'.
בעד (consonants ב-ע-ד): H1157 'for, on behalf of, behind'. Context 'for the sake of the kingdom' fits perfectly. Chose H1157.
מלכות: H4438 'a rule/dominion/kingdom' vs כות H3575 'Cuth'. Context demands 'kingdom'. Chose H4438.
יהוה: H3068 vs H3069, both refer to the divine name. Chose H3068 as the primary entry.
textual_notes: יניח appears to be hifil imperfect of נוח (H3240, 'to cause to rest, to leave, to set down'). This is not listed among candidates but is the clear verbal form.

בתי דירתו ('houses of his dwelling') is an unusual phrase. דירתו does not appear in the Strong's lexicon directly; it appears to be a noun דירה ('dwelling/residence') with 3ms suffix, suggesting a later Hebrew or medieval Hebrew term.
The sentence beginning 'no human will leave... for the sake of the kingdom of YHWH' appears to continue into the next section, suggesting this is an incomplete clause (protasis of a conditional).

verses.literal: And-Yeshua said to-them truth I [am]-saying to-you no human not will-leave his-father and-his-mother or his-brothers or his-wife or his-sons or houses-of his-dwelling for the-sake-of [the]-kingdom-of YHWH

verses.translation: who will not receive more and more than what [he] left in this time [or: age], and in the world [or: age] to come, everlasting life [or: life eternal].

translation_notes: שלא: ש (relative particle 'who/that') + לא H3808 ('not'). Together: 'who not' or 'that not'. Contextually this completes the conditional from section 4: 'no one who leaves... who will not receive more.'
ממה: מן ('from') + מה H4100 ('what'). 'From what' = 'than what'.
בזמן: Candidates: H2163 'to fix a time', H2164 'to agree on a time', H2165 'an appointed occasion', H2166 (Aramaic). Chose H2165 as the noun 'time/appointed occasion' fits with the prepositional ב.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. 'In time this' = 'in this time'. Chose H2088.
חיים: Not listed with candidates but consonants ח-י-י-ם clearly correspond to H2416 'life/alive'. The ים suffix here is intensifying — 'life in its fullness' — as indicated by the singular concept.
נצחיים: Root נצח (H5331, 'perpetuity/everlasting') with adjectival ים suffix. 'Everlasting/eternal'.
textual_notes: The < before הניח likely indicates a textual note or uncertain letter. The verb appears to be hifil perfect of נוח (H3240), 'he left/set aside', continuing from section 4.

שלא could be parsed as ש + לא ('who not') creating a double negative with the preceding section's לא, yielding 'no one... who will not receive' = 'everyone will receive'. This is the most natural reading.

verses.translation: And Yeshua took [aside] his twelve disciples and said to them, "Behold, we [are] going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written by [or: concerning] the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled [or: completed]."

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction'. Verb fits the narrative action of taking aside disciples. Chose H3947.
שנים: H8147 'two/twofold'. Combined with עשר = 'twelve'.

עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 'ten (in combination, -teen)'. With שנים, this forms 'twelve'. Chose H6240 which is the combining form used for numbers 11-19.
הנה: Same as section 3. Interjection 'behold'. Chose H2009.
בעד: H1157 'for, behind, concerning'. In context 'written by/concerning the prophets'. Chose H1157.
שבן: ש (relative 'that') + בן H1121 'son'. Together 'that the son of'. Chose H1121.
האדם: Candidates same as before. 'The human/the man' — forming the title 'Son of Man'. Chose H120.
ואמר: H559 'to say'. Narrative speech verb. Chose H559.
textual_notes: בעד הנביאים could mean 'by the prophets' (agency) or 'concerning the prophets' or 'through the prophets'. The most natural reading in context of 'things written' is 'by/through the prophets'.

שבן האדם: The placement at the end is ambiguous — it could be the subject of 'will be completed' (all the things written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be completed) or could begin a new clause. The former reading is more coherent.
תלמידיו is a post-biblical Hebrew word (from למד 'to learn') not found in the Strong's lexicon, indicating a later Hebrew text.

verses.translation: He will be handed over [or: delivered] to the peoples [or: nations], and upon him they will bring out mockery [or: scorn], and he will be oppressed [or: driven hard] and afflicted, and they will spit in his face.

translation_notes: לעג (consonants ל-ע-ג): Candidates: H3932 'to deride/mock', H3933 'derision/scoffing', H3934 'a buffoon/foreigner'. Context 'they will bring out mockery upon him' requires a noun. Chose H3933 'derision/scoffing'.

נגש (consonants נ-ג-ש): Candidates: H5065 'to drive/oppress/tyrannize', H5066 'to come near/approach'. In context of suffering and affliction, 'oppressed/driven' fits the parallel with 'afflicted'. Chose H5065.
textual_notes: ונענה could be from ענה H6031 ('to afflict/humble') in nifal ('he will be afflicted') or from ענה H6030 ('to answer/respond'). The suffering context strongly favors 'afflicted'.
וירוקו could be from רקק H7556 ('to spit') or from ירק H3417 ('to spit'). Both yield the same meaning. The waw-consecutive + imperfect form suggests 'and they will spit'.

verses.translation: And when he has been oppressed [or: scourged], they will kill him, and on the third day he will return alive.

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. With prefix וכ, this reads 'and as/when'. Chose H834.
וביום: H3117 'a day' vs H3118 'a day (Aramaic)'. Hebrew context. Chose H3117.
חי: Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 'alive (Aramaic)'. Hebrew context. Chose H2416.
textual_notes: נגוש appears to be a passive participle from נגש H5065 ('oppressed/driven'). It could also be parsed as a noun form, but the passive participle reading is most natural with יהיה.
ה<לישי: The < suggests a textual uncertainty or damaged letter. The word clearly reads השלישי ('the third') from H7992.
יחזור is not a standard biblical Hebrew form but is common in later Hebrew, from חזר ('to return'). This confirms the text is in a later stratum of Hebrew.

verses.literal: And-as-when he-will-be oppressed they-will-kill-him and-on-day the-third he-will-return alive

verses.translation: And they did not understand any thing of these [words]. This matter was hidden from them, and they did not understand what it was.

translation_notes: והם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they'. Context demands pronoun 'they'. Chose H1992.
שום: Same as section 4. Used as indefinite determiner 'any'; with negative אינם = 'not any' = 'no'. Chose H7760.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a noun following שום, 'any thing/word'. Chose H1697.

מאלו: מן + אלו. Candidates: H431 'lo!', H432 'if'. However, אלו in later Hebrew functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these'. Chose H431 loosely, but the actual function is demonstrative 'from these'.
זה: H2088 'this/that' vs H2089 'sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun in context. Chose H2088.
הדבר: Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1697 'word/matter'. 'This the-matter' requires the common noun. Chose H1697.
היה: Candidates: H1961 'to be/become', H1962 'ruin'. 'Was hidden' requires the copula. Chose H1961.
מהם: מן + הם H1992 'them'. 'From them'.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Pronoun 'it' completing 'what it [was]'. Chose H1931.
מבינים: Listed candidate H3241 'Janim (place)' matches only ינים, not the full מבינים. The word is clearly a hifil participle of בין H995 ('to discern/understand'). Chose H995.
textual_notes: The ' mark between נעלם and מהם may indicate a textual break, damaged section, or scribal notation.
מאלו uses a demonstrative form (אלו 'these') typical of later/Mishnaic Hebrew rather than biblical Hebrew אלה.
אינם is a negative existential particle + 3mp suffix ('they are not'), common in later Hebrew but not listed in the Strong's system.

verses.translation: And it happened, as [or: when] Yeshua drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man [was] sitting near the road, asking the passers-by [that] they would give to him.

translation_notes: כאשר: Same as section 8. כ + אשר H834 'when/as'. Chose H834.
ישוע: H3442 vs H3443, both 'Jeshua'. Chose H3442 as primary entry.
קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach/draw near', H7127 (Aramaic), H7128 'hostile encounter', H7129 (Aramaic), H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. As a verb 'drew near', chose H7126.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. As a numeral/indefinite article modifying 'blind man', chose H259.
לדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread/walk', H1870 'a road/path'. With preposition ל, the noun reading 'to/near the road' is natural. Chose H1870.

שואל: The candidate list for אל gives H408-H413 (various), but שואל is clearly a participle from שאל H7592 ('to ask/request/beg'). The consonants ש-א-ל point to the verb, not to the preposition אל with prefix.
עיור: Not directly in candidates but consonants ע-ו-ר correspond to H5787 (עִוֵּר, 'blind'). The י may be a mater lectionis.
textual_notes: ונעשה could be parsed as nifal of עשה H6213 ('and it was done/happened') or as 'and we will do' (1cp cohortative). The narrative third-person context strongly favors 'and it happened'.
שואל could theoretically be parsed as ש + אל ('that to'), but the participial reading 'asking/begging' is far more natural in the scene of a blind beggar by the road.

The sentence structure suggests the blind man was both sitting and begging — asking passers-by to give to him. The verb יתנו (imperfect 3mp of נתן) functions as a subjunctive: '[that] they would give'.

verses.literal: And-it-happened as-when Yeshua drew-near to-Jericho [a]-blind-one one sitting near to-the-road asking to-the-passers-by [that]-they-give to-him

verses.translation: And when the blind man heard that a great crowd [or: multitude] was passing by, he asked what this [was]

translation_notes: העור (consonants ע-ו-ר): Candidates: H5782 'to wake', H5783 'to be bare', H5784 'chaff', H5785 'skin', H5786 'to blind', H5787 'blind'. Chose H5787 because with the article ה this is a substantive adjective 'the blind one' — a person who hears a crowd passing and asks about it, which fits blindness perfectly.
עם (consonants ע-מ): Candidates: H5971 'a people/crowd', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because it pairs with רב to form 'great crowd' — a blind person hearing a large group passing by.

רב (consonants ר-ב): Candidates: H7227 'abundant/great', H7228 'archer', H7229 'abundant', H7230 'abundance'. Chose H7227 because 'great people/crowd' is the natural description of what the blind man hears passing.
textual_notes: שעובר appears to be the relative particle ש + עובר (participle of עבר, to pass over/through). No Strong's candidates were provided for this compound form.

verses.literal: And when the blind [one] heard that [a] people great [was] passing, he asked what [is] this
And they said to him that Yeshua who [is] of Nazareth [is] passing in that place
verses.amplified: And they told him that Yeshua [Jesus] of Nazareth was passing through that place [or: that very spot]
work: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'a brand or scar', H3588 'relative conjunction/adverb — that, because, for'. Chose H3588 because this word introduces a reported speech clause ('they said to him THAT...'), which is the standard function of כי as a conjunction.

ישוע (YShW'): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua — proper name', H3443 same meaning (Aramaic form). Chose H3442 because both refer to the same name; H3442 is the primary Hebrew entry for this proper noun.

די (DY): Candidates: H1767 'enough, sufficiency', H1768 'that, who, which (relative particle, Aramaic)'. Chose H1768 because here it functions as a relative particle linking 'Yeshua' to 'Nazareth' — 'Yeshua who [is] of Nazareth.' This is consistent with Aramaic-influenced Hebrew usage.

מקום (MQWM): Candidates: H4725 'place, standing spot, locality', H6965/H6966 'to rise' (root קום). Chose H4725 because the מ- prefix plus קום forms the noun 'place/location,' and the sentence requires a noun here ('in that place'), not a verb.
ambiguities: The words ואמרו (and they said), לו (to him), נצרת (Nazareth), עובר (passing), and באותו (in that) lack Strong's candidates in the provided data. ואמרו is clearly from אמר (H559, to say) in 3mp completed form with vav-consecutive. לו is the preposition ל with 3ms suffix. נצרת is the proper noun Nazareth. עובר is a participle from עבר (H5674, to pass/cross over). באותו is the preposition ב plus a demonstrative pronoun 'that' — likely a later Hebrew form (אותו).
די could also be read as H1767 'enough/sufficiency,' which would yield 'Yeshua — enough of Nazareth — passes by,' a nonsensical reading. H1768 as a relative particle is clearly correct in context.

verses.translation: And the blind man cried out, 'Yeshua [Jesus], son of David, have compassion [or: mercy] upon me!'

translation_notes: והעור (consonants ע-ו-ר): Same as section 1. Chose H5787 'blind' — the blind man from the narrative is now crying out.
קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out/address by name', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call out', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7121 because the blind man is calling out/crying aloud to Yeshua by name.
דוד: Candidates: H1730 'love/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 because 'son of David' is a title directed at Yeshua.

עלי: Candidates: H5940 'pestle', H5941 'Eli', H5942 'high', H5943 'supreme'. However, the consonants על + pronominal suffix י naturally read 'upon me'. This is a prepositional phrase, not one of the listed nouns.
textual_notes: רחמנות is a later Hebrew abstract noun form (from root ר-ח-מ 'to have compassion') not directly listed in the Strong's candidates. It clearly means 'compassion/mercy'.
עלי could theoretically be a proper noun (Eli) or the preposition 'upon me'. Context demands 'upon me' as part of the plea for mercy.

verses.literal: And the blind [one] called out Yeshua son [of] David let there be to you compassion upon me

verses.translation: And those who were walking with him rebuked [or: cursed] him [telling him] to be silent, but he, the blind man, cried out all the more, 'Son of David, have compassion upon me!'

translation_notes: והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'and he, the blind one' is a contrastive subject pronoun introducing the blind man's defiant response.
עור: Same consonants as before. Chose H5787 'blind' — continuing the narrative about the blind man.

חמול: The sole candidate H2538 is 'Chamul, an Israelite' (proper name). However, the root ח-מ-ל means 'to have compassion/spare' (cf. H2550 חמל). In context this is an imperative 'have compassion!' directed at the son of David. The consonants support the verb חמול as an imperative of חמל.
עלי: As in section 3, this reads as the preposition 'upon me' rather than any of the listed noun candidates.
textual_notes: חמול: The only Strong's candidate provided is H2538 (proper name Chamul). But the root חמל (H2550, 'to spare/have compassion') produces the imperative form חמול. This is clearly the intended reading contextually — a plea for mercy — though the specific Strong's number for the verb was not among the candidates.
מקללין could derive from קלל 'to curse' or in later usage 'to rebuke/scold'. In this narrative context, 'rebuking' or 'scolding' him to be silent is the most natural sense.

verses.literal: And those that [are] walking with him [are] cursing him that he be silent and he [the] blind [one] more [is] crying out son [of] David have compassion upon me

verses.translation: And Yeshua [Jesus] stood still and commanded that they bring the blind man to him. And when they had brought him before him, he asked him,

translation_notes: עמד: Candidates: H5975 'to stand', H5976 'to shake', H5977 'a spot', H5978 'along with'. Chose H5975 because Yeshua stopping and standing still before issuing a command is the natural narrative action.
וכאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר include H834 'who/which/when'. Chose H834 as temporal conjunction 'and when' — introducing the next action in sequence.

שאלו: The consonants could include שאל (H7592 'to ask') + suffix ו. Chose this reading because Yeshua asks the blind man a question (section 6 provides the question). The listed candidates H431/H432 for אלו do not fit.
textual_notes: הץביאוהו appears to be a scribal variant or error for הביאוהו ('they brought him'). The צ may be a copying artifact. The hiphil form of בוא with 3ms suffix is the intended reading.
שאלו could be parsed as ש + אלו ('that those') or as שאל + ו ('he asked him'). Context strongly favors 'he asked him' since section 6 immediately gives the content of the question.

verses.translation: What do you desire [or: want] that I do for you? And he said, 'Master [or: Lord], that I might see [or: be one who sees].'

translation_notes: אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'what do you desire' requires a second person pronoun as subject.
חפץ: Candidates: H2654 'to incline/be pleased/desire', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 because this is a verb form — 'what do you desire that I do for you?'
אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'he said' is the standard dialogue marker.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 because the blind man addresses Yeshua as 'lord/master'.

verses.translation: And Yeshua [Jesus] said to him, 'See! Your faithfulness [or: trust, faith] has saved [or: will deliver] you.'

translation_notes: ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'bird of prey', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 as an imperative 'see!' — both a command and profoundly fitting since the blind man is being granted sight. The double meaning (imperative 'see!' and the actual granting of sight) is striking.
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard dialogue introduction.
textual_notes: אץמונתך appears to be a scribal variant for אמונתך ('your faith/faithfulness'), with an extra צ as a copying artifact. The root is א-מ-נ (H530 אמונה 'faithfulness/faith') with 2ms possessive suffix.

תושיע is a hiphil imperfect 3fs of ישע ('to save/deliver'), with 'your faithfulness' as the subject. It could also be read as 2fs — but the subject 'your faithfulness' taking a feminine verb makes better grammatical sense.

verses.translation: And immediately he saw, and he walked [or: followed] after Yeshua [Jesus], praising [or: glorifying] YHWH [the LORD].

translation_notes: ומיד: The מ prefix + יד (H3027 'hand'). The idiom מיד means 'from hand' i.e. 'immediately/at once'. This is the standard Hebrew expression for immediacy.

ראה: Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'experiencing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 because the blind man, having been told 'see!', now actually sees — the narrative fulfillment.
והלך: Candidates: H1980 'to walk', H1981 'to walk', H1982 'a journey/wayfarer', H1983 'a journey/toll'. Chose H1980 because 'he walked after Yeshua' describes the man following him.
משבח: Candidates: H7623 'to address in a loud tone/praise', H7624 'to adulate/adore'. Chose H7623 because 'praising YHWH' in a loud voice fits the joyous response of a man just healed of blindness.
ליהוה: Candidates: H3068 'YHWH', H3069 'YHWH'. Chose H3068 as the primary form of the divine name.
textual_notes: אחרי: The sole candidate provided is H317 'other'. However, the consonants אחרי naturally read as the preposition 'after/behind' (typically identified as H310 אחרי). Context demands 'after Yeshua' — he followed behind him.

verses.literal: And from hand he saw and he walked after Yeshua praising YHWH
